newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: UBS optimistic but provisions still high.
newsitem.headline: UBS optimistic but provisions still high.

text.p: Union Bank of Switzerland (UBS) said it remained cautiously optimistic for its results for the entire 1996 year, but also noted that provisions remained higher than expected.

It said that its third-quarter results were weaker compared with the first two quarters, but that its cash flow and group profit for the first nine months were above the same figure of the first nine months of 1995.
"Provisions for credit risks continued to be higher than expected," it said in a press statement to announce its nine-month results.
The statement contained no absolute amounts, and also gave few percentage comparisons versus previous periods.

"As anticipated, third-quarter earningns at Union Bank of Switzerland did not prove as strong as in the first half of the year, due to the usual summer lull. Overall, however, operating results for the first nine months were good," UBS said.
It said that cash flow and group profit were "not only higher than a year earlier, but were also more than 75 percent of last year's full figure."
It also added that "the mid-year comparison shows a decline in growth, however, due to developments in the markets."
The decline in the third quarter was mainly seen in trading income, "which was well below that of the first two quarters," UBS said.
"Cumulated over all three quarters, however, trading income still shows the strongest earnings growth year-on-year," UBS said.
"At end-September trading income was already higher than last year's full figure. The strongest contribution came from the equities sector," it said.

"The Group's forecast for 1996 operating profit remains cautiously optimistic. Given the market situation, group earnings can be expected to remain good. The final result, however, will ultimately depend on provisioning requirements for credit risks in Switzerland," UBS said.
